fatal_errors: It incorrectly identifies DFT simulation as the production method; the actual synthesis method is spray-drying followed by thermal decomposition-reduction in H2.
It omits the experimentally supported hydrogen-assisted sequential reduction mechanism initiated by Pt, Ir, or Ru.
It provides no synthesis parameters, precursor description, phase-control conditions, catalytic results, or supporting evidence.
It conflates a computational tool used to analyze energetics and mechanisms with the physical intervention that forms the nanoframeworks.
explanation: The hypothesis is only topically aligned with NM-HEA three-dimensional nanoframeworks. The target method is SD-TDR: homogeneous mixed salts are spray-dried into precursor particles and reduced in H2, typically at 300°C for 30 minutes, to form porous, compositionally homogeneous HEA-3DNFs. Their low-temperature formation is attributed to early reduction of Pt, Ir, or Ru, followed by H2 dissociation and reactive-hydrogen-assisted reduction and incorporation of transition metals into the noble-metal lattice. DFT supports this mechanistic interpretation and phase-transition analysis but does not itself produce the material. The proposed comparison is also too vague to discriminate this incorrect synthesis claim and lacks defined structural or catalytic thresholds.
